did_you_know.text: Did you know? Micah is described as a man from the hill country of Ephraim, and his full name in the verse is Micaiah.
Did you know? The amount Micah took from his mother was 1,100 pieces of silver. After hearing her curse, he admitted that he had taken the money and returned it to her.
Did you know? Micah’s mother said that she had dedicated the money to the LORD to make a carved image and a cast image, and then agreed to return the money to her son.
Did you know? From the 1,100 pieces of silver, the mother took 200 pieces and gave them to a silversmith, who made them into a carved image and a cast image that were kept in Micah’s house.

Did you know? Micah’s house also contained an ephod and household idols, and Micah appointed one of his sons as a priest. In this way, a private place of worship was established in his house, described as a “house of God.”
Did you know? The narrator explains the background to the events in the chapter: In those days there was no king in Israel, so everyone did what was right in his own eyes.

Did you know? The Levite who came to Micah’s house was a young man from Bethlehem in Judah, even though the Levites were not associated with one particular inheritance like the other tribes of Israel.
Did you know? The Levite left Bethlehem in Judah to find a place to live and earn a living, and on his journey he came to the hill country of Ephraim and to Micah’s house.
Did you know? Micah offered the Levite a place in his house to serve as his “father and priest.” In return, he promised him ten pieces of silver a year, clothing, and food.
Did you know? Micah regarded appointing the Levite as a priest as a sign that the LORD would prosper him, because, as he said, he now had a Levite serving as a priest in his house.
